summary: Batch embed warm-buffer credit suppressed after cross-environment failover and postback normalization
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a ~150k-record batch embedding job that consumed reserved hours but did not receive scheduled 'warm-buffer' hourly credits. Impact: customer saw a provisional charge in the mid-cycle invoice and requests a correction or provisional credit. Environment: BrightWrite is on a Dedicated pool in us-east and runs mixed-hosted/private fallback for resilience.

Observed behavior: Batch job started on Dedicated pool, briefly failed over to the customer's Private fallback (VPN), and then retried to Dedicated. Postbacks arriving at billing pipeline during the failover window were normalized with a 'probe' tag by edge-proxy. As a result, the postback-reconciler suppressed warm-buffer credit application for the hour window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a large embedding batch job (>100k records) on a Dedicated tenant configured with private fallback enabled
2) Induce a transient capacity/health signal on Dedicated to force fallback to Private for ~3-7 minutes
3) Allow automatic retry back to Dedicated (normal traffic flow resumes)
4) Inspect postbacks in the reconciler within the affected hourly window and check warm-buffer credit application logs
logs: 2024-11-14T23:10:12Z edge-proxy: request id=rw-98423 tag=probe origin=private-fallback status=200
2024-11-14T23:10:13Z reconciler: received postback id=pb-32091 meter_namespace=batch-embed tenant=brightwrite tag=probe deferred_credit_eval=true
2024-11-14T23:12:05Z reconciler: credit_evaluator skipped warm_buffer for hour=2024-11-14T23:00Z reason=tag_probe
2024-11-14T23:12:06Z billing: provisional_invoice line_item_id=li-77890 amount_usd=125.60 description=Batch embed usage
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Aisha): customer attached provisional invoice and activity export showing embed job spanning 23:05-23:18 UTC
Hypothesis 1 (Marcus): postback tag normalization in edge-proxy treats any fallback-origin as 'probe' causing reconciler logic to exclude eligible warm-buffer credits
Hypothesis 2: dedupe/fingerprint TTL during retry causes split postbacks across two reconciler runs, and one run lacks the warmup metadata
Reconciler code path: credit application requires billing_tag == 'prod' OR has explicit warmup flag in postback body; current normalized probe tag removes both
Repro attempt: replicated on staging with small batch and forced fallback; observed same suppressed credit in reconciler staging logs (reconciler PR referenced)
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/reconciler/pull/2123 normalized fallback-origin tags earlier this quarter to reduce noisy metrics — likely side-effect
Immediate mitigation idea: override reconciler to treat tag=probe + tenant in dedicated list as eligible for warm-buffer credit until fix shipped

resolution: Workaround applied: temporary reconciler whitelist logic merged to treat probe-tagged postbacks from Dedicated tenants with private-fallback enabled as eligible for warm-buffer credits (PR https://github.com/redwood/reconciler/pull/2134). Retroactive provisional credit of USD 125.60 issued to BrightWrite's account pending final invoice reconciliation. Follow-up: revert whitelist after robust fix. Next steps: schedule a small hardening change to edge-proxy tag normalization to include a billing_tag header that preserves warmup eligibility (follow-up ticket INT-1202 created).
